questions.q: Is it a fact that murder is wrong, or just an opinion? How do you know?
questions.answer: It's a fact. We can't measure right and wrong by ourselves, any more than Johnny could be "one Johnny tall"; we need a standard beyond us, and that points to God.

questions.q: Where do your ideas about right and wrong actually come from?
questions.answer: Probably home, school, friends and online. But the lesson says a sense of right and wrong is written on our hearts, which points to God as the real standard.

questions.q: If copying homework isn't wrong just "because we don't," is that a good reason?
questions.answer: No. "Because we just don't" isn't really a reason. If right and wrong are only opinion, nothing is truly wrong, so we need a standard outside ourselves.
